keyframe_review.note: 343,293 km2 for 1800-1819 (this dossier takes 1801-1819; Great Britain takes 1800). The land is the British Isles with all of Ireland, now direct ('creating the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland on 1 January 1801'), plus Gibraltar, Menorca and Malta. Size check: UK infobox 244,376 km2 (no year) plus the Irish Free State infobox 70,000 km2 (no year) is 314,376 km2, ratio 1.09. Kept as drawn; the baseline holds Menorca only until the ledger's 1802 loss. Malta was a protectorate from 1800 and became 'a colony by the Treaty of Paris in 1814' (Malta Protectorate page). Hanover (personal union 1714-1837) is not in this shape and is not UK land. Not drawn and not on any page opened: Heligoland, the Channel Islands.

keyframe_review.note: 383,810 km2: the 1800 land plus 166 cells in Germany (about 36,000 km2) and 7 cells of the Ionian Islands. The German cells are the Kingdom of Hanover, 'established in October 1814 by the Congress of Vienna' and 'in personal union with Great Britain between 1714 and 1837': a separate state under the same king, so not UK land (an association is never territory, rule 4). The Ionian Islands: 'Britain obtained a protectorate over the Ionian Islands' (Ionian Islands page, infobox area 4,696 km2 for 1864 against about 2,000 km2 of cells: the grid undercounts small islands), a vassal tint from 1815 (ledger). The protectorate tint runs to 1971 (ledger); the cells are taken out of the whole span. Gibraltar stays.

266,470 km2 against the infobox '244,376 km2 (94,354 sq mi)' (no year): ratio 1.09, fine (Cliopatria includes the Isle of Man and coastal cells). Gibraltar and the Sovereign Base Areas are missing in 2024 only; they are drawn by the british-overseas-territories row (2000-2024), as are the other overseas territories, which 'do not strictly form part of the United Kingdom'. region.text: the British Isles as one kingdom: Great Britain, the Isle of Man, Gibraltar, Menorca and Malta, with Ireland

ledger.note: 1801: Great Britain and Ireland unite as the United Kingdom. 'creating the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland on 1 January 1801'; infobox 'Acts of Union of Great Britain and Ireland: 1 January 1801'.

1801: Ireland becomes part of the United Kingdom. Infobox 'Union with Ireland: 31 December 1800'; 'Ireland remained formally separate, with its own parliament, until the Acts of Union 1800 took effect'; 'The Irish Parliament was closed down.' The vassal tint of the Great Britain dossier ends and the island is direct land.
1802: Menorca is returned to Spain. 'though they ceded it back to Spain in 1802 Treaty of Amiens' (the sentence carries a [citation needed] tag on the page).

region.text: the seven Ionian islands, 'It included seven island states'

ledger.note: 1815: the Ionian Islands become a British protectorate. 'Britain obtained a protectorate over the Ionian Islands' by the Treaty of Paris of 5 November 1815; infobox 'Protectorate established: 9 November 1815'; seven islands under a Lord High Commissioner (Corfu, Cephalonia, Cythera, Ithaca, Paxos, Lefkada, Zakynthos); Britain had taken Zakynthos and Kefalonia in 1809 and Lefkada in 1810.

January 1839: the Bombay Presidency takes Aden. 'after the conquest of Aden by the Bombay Presidency of British India in January 1839'; 'Aden Settlement (1839-1932), Aden Province (1932-1937), the Colony of Aden (1937-1963)'. The page does not name the previous ruler.

May 1864: the Ionian Islands pass to Greece. Treaty of London of 29 March 1864 'pledging the transfer of sovereignty to Greece upon ratification'; infobox 'Union with Greece: 21 May 1864' (the text gives a proclamation on 28 May and union on 2 June, so the pages disagree). The land goes to first-hellenic-republic.

4 June 1878: Britain takes Cyprus under the Cyprus Convention. 'A British protectorate under nominal Ottoman suzerainty was established over Cyprus by the Cyprus Convention of 4 June 1878'. Hatched, as the island stays Ottoman in law.
1880: Bahrain accepts British protection. The Trucial page: 'following on from Bahrain in 1880' (an agreement; its kind is not stated). Cliopatria draws the island from 1895.

region.text: the Mahra Sultanate of Qishn and Socotra

ledger.note: 1886: the Aden Protectorate begins with the Mahra. 'Beginning with a formal treaty of protection with the Mahra Sultanate of Qishn and Socotra in 1886' (the infobox gives 'Initial treaty: 1872'); the protectorate later 'extended well east of Aden to Hadhramaut'.

region.text: the rest of the hinterland: the Western Protectorate and Hadhramaut

ledger.note: 1890: the rest of the hinterland comes under protection (the year is Cliopatria's, page silent). The page names 'nine states' of informal protection (the 'Nine Tribes' or 'Nine Cantons'), a Western Protectorate of c. 55,000 km2 and an Eastern Protectorate of c. 230,000 km2 reaching Hadhramaut, but dates none of the later treaties; Cliopatria's shape grows by 1,407 cells in 1890.

region.text: the Trucial Coast: Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Fujairah and Ras Al Khaimah

ledger.note: 6-8 March 1892: the Trucial Coast comes under British protection. The Exclusive Agreement was signed 'between 6 and 8 March 1892'; 'the British promised to protect the Trucial Coast from all aggression by sea'; the status 'fell short of a formal protectorate' (the page also gives the General Maritime Treaty of 8 January 1820 and the Perpetual Maritime Truce of 4 May 1853). Cliopatria draws it from 1895.
5 November 1914: the occupation of Cyprus ends in annexation (next event).

5 November 1914: Britain annexes Cyprus. '5 November 1914, when after the Ottomans joined the Central Powers ... Britain declared the complete annexation of Cyprus into the British Empire, albeit under a military administration status'; 'The Crown Colony of Cyprus was proclaimed a decade later, in 1925'.

region.text: southern Ottoman Syria, later Mandatory Palestine

ledger.note: 1917: British forces conquer southern Ottoman Syria. 'The conquest of Ottoman Syria by British forces in 1917'; the infobox lists the predecessor as the 'Occupied Enemy Territory Administration'. The page gives no month and no boundary; Palestine west of the Jordan is the researcher's reading.

13 November 1918: British troops enter Constantinople. 'The first French troops entered the city on 12 November 1918, followed by British troops the next day'; on 16 March 1920 'the Allied forces declared the occupation' formally. Cliopatria also draws the Straits (Gallipoli, Chanak) from 1919; the page does not say the British held them as a zone.

region.text: the British occupation zone around Cologne

ledger.note: 6 December 1918: the British enter Cologne. 'Cologne was entered on 6 December, and the bridgehead was occupied 12 December'; 'The British Army of the Rhine was established as the occupying force in March 1919'; under the Treaty of Versailles 'the Cologne region (under the British) would be evacuated after five years'. The Weimar Republic follows the German Empire in 1919.

region.text: southern Ottoman Syria, later Mandatory Palestine

ledger.note: April 1920: the military occupation of Palestine gives way to the mandate (next event).

25 April 1920: Britain is assigned the mandate for Palestine. Infobox 'Mandate assigned: 25 April 1920'; 'Britain officially assumes control: 29 September 1923'; 'the British obtained a Mandate for Palestine from the League of Nations in 1922'. A mandate is administered land with its own dossier (british-mandate-for-palestine), drawn as a vassal tint.

1922: Transjordan is set apart under the mandate. 'the Trans-Jordan memorandum excluded territories of the Emirate of Transjordan from any Jewish settlement' (the memorandum carries no date on the page; the mandate is 1922). The Emirate is the Hashemite state of kingdom-of-jordan, under British tutelage until independence 'in 1946'.

6 December 1922: the Irish Free State leaves the United Kingdom. 'The Free State was established on 6 December 1922'; 'Most of Ireland seceded from the UK in 1922'; 'It comprised 26 of the 32 counties of Ireland'; 'The following day, the Commons and the Senate of Northern Ireland passed resolutions "for the express purpose of opting out of the Free State"' and 'Northern Ireland remained part of the United Kingdom'.

4 October 1923: the Allies leave Constantinople. 'Allied forces started evacuating Istanbul on 23 August 1923 and completed the task on 4 October 1923'; 'the Treaty of Lausanne, signed on 24 July 1923, led to the end of the occupation'; the Chanak Crisis 'nearly resulted in hostilities, these being avoided on 11 October 1922' (Armistice of Mudanya).

region.text: the British occupation zone around Cologne

ledger.note: January 1926: the British leave the Cologne zone. 'British troops withdrew from their zone in January 1926' (the zone was to have been vacated in January 1925; the last Allied troops left the Mainz zone on 30 June 1930).

1927: the state is renamed the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. 'the name was changed in 1927 to the "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland"'. Colour and dossier continue.

region.text: Iceland, whose king 'was still the Icelandic head of state' (the king of Denmark)

ledger.note: 10 May 1940: British forces invade Iceland. 'the British invaded on the morning of 10 May' (Operation Fork, by the Royal Navy and Royal Marines); Reykjavik 'reaffirmed its neutrality'. Hatched.

7 July 1941: the United States takes over Iceland's defence. 'the defence of Iceland was transferred from Britain to the (still officially neutral) United States' ('The US agreed on 16 June 1941'). 'At the end of hostilities most British facilities were turned over to the Icelandic government.'

region.text: the British zone: the northwest of Germany with the Ruhr (Schleswig-Holstein, Hamburg, Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia; reviewer eu-11-l replaced a 420 km circle around Hanover that covered the Soviet and American zones)

ledger.note: June 1945: Britain takes over its zone of Germany. The Berlin Declaration of 5 June 1945 began the Allied authority ('from the Berlin Declaration on 5 June 1945'); the Potsdam Agreement of 2 August 1945 divided Germany into four zones; 'The British occupation zone included the Ruhr industrial region' (Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia, Schleswig-Holstein, Hamburg); 'By May 1945' the British and Canadian armies 'had conquered Northern Germany'. Hatched.
1946: Transjordan becomes independent. 'announced the independence of the Emirate of Transjordan as the Hashemite Kingdom of Transjordan in 1946' (the page gives no day).

14/15 May 1948: the Mandate for Palestine ends. 'At midnight on 14/15 May 1948, the Mandate for Palestine expired, and the State of Israel came into being.' The land goes to the new Israel and to the neighbours in the 1948 war.

region.text: the British zone (Schleswig-Holstein, Hamburg, Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia; reviewer eu-11-l replaced a 420 km circle around Hanover that covered the Soviet and American zones)

ledger.note: 23 May 1949: the British zone merges into West Germany. 'The three western zones were merged to form the Federal Republic of Germany' (infobox 'West Germany: 23 May 1949'); 'the occupation continued until 5 May 1955', when 'the western occupation zones ceased to exist'. The zone is drawn as occupied until the Federal Republic exists.

region.text: Cyprus without the Sovereign Base Areas

ledger.note: 16 August 1960: Cyprus becomes independent. 'The United Kingdom granted independence to Cyprus on 16 August 1960 and formed the Republic of Cyprus'; 'the United Kingdom retained possession of the Sovereign Base Areas of Akrotiri and Dhekelia as a British Overseas Territory' (the british-overseas-territories row).

minus.text: the Aden Protectorate hinterland: the cells Cliopatria adds in 1890 and its eastern fringe
the Mahra Sultanate of Qishn and Socotra

region.text: the rest of the hinterland: the Western Protectorate and Hadhramaut

ledger.note: November 1967: the Aden Protectorate ends with the British departure. 'the British leaving Aden by the end of November 1967' (the page gives the Federation of Arab Emirates of the South on 11 February 1959 and the Federation of South Arabia on 18 January 1963). The land goes to the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen (Cliopatria row from 1969).

region.text: the Mahra Sultanate of Qishn and Socotra

ledger.note: November 1967: the Mahra lands leave British protection with the rest of the Protectorate ('the British leaving Aden by the end of November 1967').

November 1967: the Colony of Aden is given up. 'the British leaving Aden by the end of November 1967'; 'the Colony of Aden (1937-1963)' merged into the Federation of South Arabia on 18 January 1963. The page does not give the independence day.

1971: Bahrain's British tie ends (page silent on Bahrain itself). The Trucial page only says 'Bahrain and Qatar dropped out of talks' before the July 1971 union agreement; Cliopatria gives the Kingdom of Bahrain a row from 1973. The year bridges the silence.

1 December 1971: the Trucial treaties end and the Emirates become the United Arab Emirates. 'until the treaties were revoked on 1 December 1971'; infobox 'United Arab Emirates: 2 December 1971'; the withdrawal of all British troops had been announced on 16 January 1968; Ras Al Khaimah 'joined on 10 February 1972'.

wars.name: Napoleonic Wars
wars.outcome: Britain took Zakynthos and Kefalonia (1809) and Lefkada (1810) and obtained 'a protectorate over the Ionian Islands' by the Treaty of Paris of 5 November 1815; Malta was confirmed by the 1814 Treaty of Paris.
wars.note: The Ionian page dates only the 1809-1810 captures and the 1815 treaty; the span is that of the Ionian operations, not of the wars (the Kingdom of Great Britain page has 'The long bitter wars with France 1793-1815').

wars.name: World War I
wars.outcome: Cyprus annexed after the Ottomans 'joined the Central Powers' (5 November 1914), southern Syria conquered in 1917, Constantinople and the Cologne zone occupied after the Armistice of 11 November 1918.
wars.note: The years are those of the events on the pages opened (Cyprus page for 1914, Rhineland page for the Armistice); the western and Macedonian fronts in Cliopatria's 1915-1918 shapes are not covered by any page opened.

wars.name: Chanak Crisis

zones.text: the neutral zone of the Straits

wars.outcome: 'The British decided to resist any attempt to penetrate the neutral zone of the Straits'; the crisis 'nearly resulted in hostilities, these being avoided on 11 October 1922' (Armistice of Mudanya). The occupation ended on 4 October 1923.

wars.name: World War II

zones.text: the British zone of Germany from 1945

wars.outcome: British occupation of Iceland ('Operation Fork', 10 May 1940) handed to the United States on 7 July 1941; the British zone of Germany from June 1945.
wars.note: The UK page: 'After Nazi Germany's invasion of Poland in 1939, Britain entered the Second World War.'

wars.name: Jebel Akhdar War
wars.outcome: No border moved: the Imam Ghalib Bin Ali 'started an uprising in 1954'; 'In 1957, British forces bombarded the town of Nizwa'; 'the last rebel forces were defeated two years later, in 1959'. Oman stayed a 'De jure sovereign state'.
wars.note: Listed because Cliopatria draws all of Oman as UK land from 1956; the war shows British forces in Oman, not British rule.

certainty.note: The coast, the Irish border from 1922 and the enclaves (Gibraltar, Malta, Aden, Cyprus after 1914) are fixed lines. The protectorate frontiers of southern Arabia and the Trucial Coast (1886-1971) were never surveyed and are soft, and the occupations (Cologne, Constantinople, Iceland, the German zone) are tints, not borders.

notes: Written for batch eu-11-l. This is the second half of Cliopatria's single 'Kingdom of Great Britain' row (1709-2024), split at the union of 1 January 1801; the Great Britain half is kingdom-of-great-britain. Fourteen pages of its own (budget 14: UK, Irish Free State, Hanover, Aden Protectorate, Trucial States, Mandatory Palestine, Muscat and Oman, British Cyprus, Ionian Islands, Allied-occupied Germany, Occupation of Iceland, Occupation of the Rhineland, Allied occupation of Constantinople, List of British monarchs) plus three shared with the Great Britain dossier (Kingdom of Great Britain, Menorca, Malta Protectorate). WHAT THE CLIOPATRIA ROW IS: from 1801 it is the UK plus a changing set of other people's land: Hanover (1820-1852), the Ionian Islands (1820-1869), the Aden hinterland (1890-1968), the Trucial Coast and Bahrain (1895-2023), Cyprus (1880-1968), the Rhineland and the Straits (1919-1926), Palestine and Transjordan (1936-1947), Iceland (1940-1944), the German zone (1945-1946), Oman (1920-2023) and the Gulf (Kuwait 1932-1968, Qatar 1936-2023). Rule 4 treats protectorates and occupations as tints and an association (a personal union) as never territory, so each keyframe correction is the Cliopatria shape minus the lands the pages show were not UK territory, and the ledger carries the vassal and occupation events. UNVERIFIED (page budget): the Crimea cell (1856-1858), the Western Front cells (1915-1916), the Aegean islands (1917-1918), Macedonia (1918), Kuwait (1932-1968), Qatar (1936-1968), the Faroes (1941-1944) and Austria (1945-1946) stay as drawn; each is flagged in its keyframe. Qatar and Bahrain are removed from 1969 because Cliopatria itself gives them rows from 1973. Heligoland, the Channel Islands and Malta's independence are not covered by any page opened; Malta stays to Cliopatria's 1968 end. HANOVER: personal union 1714-1837 ('in personal union with Great Britain between 1714 and 1837'); Cliopatria draws Hanover as UK land 1820-1839 only; it is not drawn here and no event is recorded, because an association is never territory. IRELAND: 1801 gain from kingdom-of-ireland and 1922 loss to irish-free-state; the Treaty ports and the 1925 Boundary Commission are not on the Free State page, and the war of 1919-1921 is not named there, so no war entry for it. IDENTITY: wikidata Q145 is the UK's well-known Wikidata id, not Cliopatria's (its row carries Q23666, the island); Wikidata was unreachable. The end year 2024 follows the Cliopatria convention for states alive today. Successors are empty; the Irish Free State, the dominions and the colonies take land by loss events. Counterparts needing dossiers: united-states-of-the-ionian-islands, aden-protectorate (both written in this batch from pages already opened) and house-of-khalifa (Bahrain 1783-1971; only the Al Madhkur dossier 1753-1783 exists). Region names the gazetteer lacks: none unresolved with --resolve; Menorca is a radius and the Sovereign Base Areas are two 12 km radii at 32.95 E 34.62 N and 33.75 E 34.98 N (coordinates are geography, not from a page). REVIEW eu-11-l (2026-10-25): the Bahrain counterpart was renamed bahrain-under-the-al-khalifa -> house-of-khalifa (the me-10 dossier for Bahrain 1783-1971); the British zone of Germany in /ledger/25, /ledger/28 and the World War II zone is now the four Laender of the zone (Allied-occupied Germany page) instead of a 420 km circle.
